content.user_title: Migrate Motoko Actors With Enhanced Migration Chains
content.value_statement: Motoko canister upgrades can fail or lose data when state changes do not match migration inputs and outputs. This skill guides compatible changes, self-contained migrations, and validation for enhanced migration chains.
actual_capabilities: Classify actor state changes as implicit or explicit migrations within enhanced migration projects.
Guide self-contained migration modules with inlined old and new stable types.
Explain stable subtyping, field renames, intentional removals, and state transformations.
Provide Motoko patterns for records, variants, maps, and optional fields.
Explain timestamp ordering, applied migration immutability, and the single pending migration limit.
Guide compatibility checks with mops check --fix, deployed stable signatures, and a final mops build.
limitations: The guidance targets enhanced migration chains, not legacy persistence or plain actors without a chain.
The declared toolchain requires moc 1.11.2 or newer and mops core 2.5.0 or newer.
Compatibility depends on project configuration and deployed state; this documentation alone cannot verify a live canister.
Defaults and intentional data removal require developer review, compilation, and upgrade testing.

use_cases.title: Understand stable state changes
use_cases.description: Classify proposed field changes and identify when an enhanced migration file is necessary.

use_cases.title: Write a migration module
use_cases.description: Draft self-contained state transformations while preserving unchanged fields and using the existing pending migration.

use_cases.title: Review upgrade readiness
use_cases.description: Check chain ordering, deployed signatures, intentional data removal, and validation steps before releasing an upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a state change
prompt_templates.prompt: My project uses enhanced Motoko migrations. Classify these stable field changes as implicit or explicit: [changes]. Explain each decision.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a new field
prompt_templates.prompt: Add this stable field in my enhanced migration project: [field and type]. Review [existing chain] and propose initialization without modifying applied migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Transform stored records
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [old fields], [new fields], and [business rules], draft a self-contained Motoko migration. Preserve unchanged state and explain every default and discarded field.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an upgrade plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [migration plan], [deployed signature], and [mops configuration]. Check stable compatibility, chain ordering, pending limits, fresh installation, and data preservation. Propose validation steps.

output_examples.input: An enhanced migration project adds an optional assignee field to every stored task.
output_examples.output: Use an explicit migration that preserves existing task values and initializes each assignee as absent. Extend the pending migration if one already exists.

output_examples.input: A canister changes a stable numeric field from Nat to Int.
output_examples.output: This is usually a stable-compatible widening and does not need an explicit migration. Confirm the deployed signature and run the compatibility check.

output_examples.input: A canister renames artist to artists and changes the value from text to a set.
output_examples.output: Transform the old text value into a single-item set for the renamed field. Inline both state types and preserve all unrelated fields.

best_practices: Derive old state from the preceding migration; use empty state only for a new chain, not a legacy conversion.
Keep applied migrations unchanged and fold new work into the pending file.
Run compatibility checks before building and test the upgrade with representative state.
anti_patterns: Do not add a migration for a stable-compatible change or an identity transformation.
Do not apply the enhanced-chain initializer rules to plain actors without a migration chain.
Do not import project types into frozen migration files or discard fields unintentionally.

faq.question: When is an explicit migration required?
faq.answer: In enhanced migration projects, use one for renamed, removed, narrowed, transformed, or newly added stable fields.

faq.question: Can I change field mutability without a migration?
faq.answer: Yes. Changing var to let, or the reverse, is usually stable-compatible.

faq.question: Where should migration files live?
faq.answer: Read the chain directory in mops.toml. The default location in this guide is src/backend/migrations/.

faq.question: Why must migration types be inlined?
faq.answer: Project type imports can change and invalidate historical transformations. Inline old and new types; core and mops package imports are permitted.

faq.question: How do I initialize a new stable field?
faq.answer: Under enhanced migration, declare its type in the actor and supply its value from the migration output. Plain actors follow different initialization rules.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy my canister?
faq.answer: It does not include a deployment script. It guides migration authoring, compatibility checks, and builds; deployment still requires your project workflow.
